sentences.text:
Munni Lal Sahu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6
November, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:28104
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Gwalior

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Ashish Shroti

On The 6 th Of November, 2025
 Writ Petition No. 17801 of 2022
 Munni Lal Sahu
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri D.P.Singh - Advocate for the petitioner.
 Shri Naval Kishor Gupta - Ga for the respondents/State
 Order

Petitioner is aggrieved by the order dated 7/4/2022 (Annexure P/1), whereby, the amount of his gratuity has been withheld by the respondents relying upon Rule 64(c) of the M.P. Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1976 (for short "Pension Rules").
2. Facts necessary for decision of this case are that petitioner was working as Assistant Engineer in the respondent/Department.

He retired from service w.e.f. 31/7/2021.While the petitioner was in service, a criminal case was instituted against him alongwith other co-accused persons for offence punishment under Sections 409, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B of IPC and Section 13(1)(d) and 13 (2) of Prevention of Corruption Act.
Trial is pending before the Court.
On account of pendency of the aforesaid criminal case, the entire amount of gratuity of the petitioner has been withheld relying upon Rule 64 (c) of the Pension Rules.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28104 2 WP-17801-2022 3.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the respondents have placed reliance upon Rule 64 (c) of the Pension Rules, which was amended vide notification dated 19/5/2023.
It is his submission that the petitioner stood retired w.e.f. 31/7/2021, and therefore, the rule which were prevailing on the date of his retirement, is required to be applied.
He further submitted that the respondent/Authority erred in relying upon the aforesaid rule in its order dated 7/4/2022, which had come into force in future on 19/5/2023.

In support of his submissions, he placed reliance upon the decision of this Court in the case of Tarachand Kanvjiya Vs. State of M.P. & Ors., in W.P.No.
20450/2023.

sentences.text: On the other hand, counsel for the State supported the impugned action of the respondents and submitted that since the petitioner is facing criminal trial for a serious offence, particularly under the Prevention of Corruption Act, he is not entitled to the amount of gratuity as per Rule 64 (c) of the Pension Rules.
He further submitted that the remaining retiral dues of the petitioner including Family Benefit Fund, GIS, GPF, Leave Encashment, etc., have already been paid to the petitioner.

In addition, he is being paid provisional pension at the rate of 64,000/- plus dearness allowances,
which was sanctioned to him vide order dated 11/10/2021.

He thus, submits that the action of respondent/authority is inconsonance with the Rule 64 (c) of the Pension Rules, and therefore, no interference is warranted in the present writ petition.
5. Considered the arguments and perused the record.
6.

The only issue involved in this case for consideration of this Court NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:28104 3 WP-17801-2022 is as to whether, the amended Rule 64(c) of the Pension Rules is applicable in the present case or not ?
7. It is not in dispute that the petitioner retired from service w.e.f. 31/7/2021.
The provisions of Rule 64(c) of Pension Rules were amended vide notification dated 19/5/2023 i.e. after the petitioner's retirement.

This Court has dealt with the similar issue in the case of Tarachand Kanvjiya (supra),
wherein, in para 6, this Court has as under:-
"6. Admittedly, the petitioner retired from service w.e.f. September' 2022.

Therefore,
payment of his retiral dues would be governed by the provisions as existing on the date of his retirement.
The learned petitioner's counsel is right in submitting that amendment incorporated subsequently in the pension rules would not effect petitioner's right to get the amount of gratuity.
It is seen that the provisions of Rule 64 of the Pension Rules has been amended w.e.f. 19/05/2023.
By virtue of clause 64(1)(c), the gratuity is not payable to the retired employee until conclusion of departmental or judicial proceedings.

However, this provision since was not available on the date of retirement of the petitioner, issue of payment of gratuity to the petitioner would be governed by the provisions of Rule 64 as existed at the time of petitioner's retirement i.e. prior to this amendment.
Needless to mention, under the unamended Rule 64, the employee was entitled to get provisional gratuity."

8. In view of the aforesaid, since the petitioner already stood retired prior to amendment in Rule 64 of the Pension Rules, the case of petitioner shall be governed by the unamended provisions of Rule 64 of Pension Rules prevailing at the time of petitioner's retirement.
9. Considering the aforesaid, order dated 7/4/2022 (Annexure P/1) is hereby set aside.

The respondents are directed to take a decision regarding payment of gratuity to petitioner in view of unamended provisions of Rule 64 of the Pension Rules as was existing on the date of is retirement i.e. on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28104 4 WP-17801-2022 31/7/2021.
Let needful be done within a period of 90 days from the date of communication of certified copy of this order.
